title: Of Gods and Glamour: The Mary and Michael Jaharis Galleries of Greek, Roman, and Byzantine Art
description: Through over 250 works, these stunning galleries present the origins and early development of Western art from the third millennium BC to the time of the great Byzantine Empire.

title: Monet and Chicago
description: The first exhibition to explore the unique connection between the city and the “Father of Impressionism” brings together over 60 paintings, including beloved major works as well as rarely seen still lifes, landscapes, and portraits of the artist's family.

title: Rembrandt Portraits
description: Two rarely loaned works from the Norton Simon Museum, a spectacular self-portrait and Portrait of a Boy, join the museum’s iconic Rembrandt paintings for a focused look at the artist’s fluid approach to portraiture.

title: Gauguin: Artist as Alchemist
description: This exhibition takes an in-depth look at Post-Impressionist Paul Gauguin's creative process and how he challenged cultural, geographic, and material boundaries.

title: Van Gogh's Bedrooms
description: Presented only at the Art Institute, this exhibition is the first dedicated to the artist's three "Bedroom" paintings, presenting an in-depth study of their making and meaning to Van Gogh.

title: Manet and the Sea
description: This landmark exhibition is devoted to the marine paintings of Edouard Manet (1832–1883), a little-studied but highly significant aspect of the career of the artist who is sometimes referred to as the father of Impressionism.

title: Cezanne
description: This groundbreaking retrospective sheds new light not only on how this pivotal artist created his works, but also why his art remains so vital today.

title: Rodin: Sculptor and Storyteller
description: This focused exhibition brings together sculptures and drawings from private collections and the museum’s holdings to explore the artist’s creative process and his narrative skill.

title: Toulouse-Lautrec and Montmartre
description: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec (1864–1901), one of the most popular and important painters of late-19th-century Paris, has not been the subject of a major exhibition since the large retrospective presented in London and Paris in 1991 and 1992. The National Gallery of Art and the Art Institute of Chicago have collaborated to organize Toulouse-Lautrec and Montmartre, an exhibition that places the artist's work at the peak of his career between 1888 and 1896 in conjunction with the work of other artists of the period.

title: Whistler's Mother: An American Icon Returns to Chicago
description: Whistler’s iconic painting returns to Chicago for the first time in over 60 years in a focused installation of 25 objects: paintings, prints, drawings, posters, and other ephemera.

title: El Greco: Ambition and Defiance
description: Featuring over 57 works that trace the singular career of the artist known as El Greco, this major exhibition considers the astounding ambition that drove him to develop his remarkable style and to continually reinvent his practice in pursuit of success.

title: Mary Cassatt: After Impressionism
description: The first Art Institute exhibition dedicated to the artist in more than 25 years showcases 70 paintings and works on paper from the late 1880s through the early 1900s, a pivotal period when she pursued some of her most ambitious and experimental work.
